explanation: In autosomal (non-sex) chromosomes, monosomy and trisomy are usually lethal to the developing organism, though trisomies generally offer a slightly better chance of survival. In humans, only three autosomal trisomies are viable beyond birth: Trisomy 13, Trisomy 18, and Trisomy 21. Among these three, Trisomy 21 is the only one that is survivable beyond childhood; this condition is known as Down Syndrome.
